Peer view: TDG’s FY2024 operating margin and cash generation exceed this selected historical cohort, but its borrowing-plus-finance-lease/CFO burden is substantially higher. Strong operations do not establish peer-like financial risk or distributable cash. HEICO is the closest operating analogue; Curtiss-Wright (CW) and Moog broaden the comparison to engineered aerospace/defense suppliers, not a representative industry distribution.

blocks.title: What changed since the last Report

runs.text: CP-2 consumption restrictions: use this checked CP-1C as a separately dated FY2024 historical overlay to the exact supplied borrower CP-1, not as replacement canonical financials. Carry two distinct findings into credit synthesis: TDG has above-cohort reported operating/cash margins in both years, yet FY2024 bridged debt/CFO is 12.166259x versus a 1.939628–4.860451x cohort range. Explain the cash-retention/distribution mechanism and the supported countercase; do not collapse them into a favorable rank.

Keep the borrower outside peer N; retain Moog in base cash/capex statistics and disclose the two exclusion sensitivities and N=2 median suppression. Preserve raw reported debt, the separate finance-lease bridge, ordinary versus restricted/held-for-sale cash, receivable-sale versus securitization funding, annual fiscal dates and subsequent events. Do not rename CFO-minus-gross-cash-capex as FCF, combine issuer EBITDA definitions, infer covenant capacity, import FY2025 valuation results, or use missing multiples as valuation/recovery/security evidence.

CP-2 must open the accepted handoff, identify its actual artifact/hash, and explicitly record which findings and limitations it consumes. No current CP-2 handoff/hash was supplied here; neither CP-2 consumption nor CP-OS/final delivery execution is claimed. Current completion is this bounded CP-1C submission only; valuation completion requires the specific evidence in T4.11.

Against that countercase, the 4,216 USDm dividend payable and historical acquisition/distribution cash demands limit an unrestricted-cash interpretation.

fields.value: Downside pathway: a demand/delivery slowdown or weaker customer funding first pressures sales absorption and working-capital cash; cash-after-capex then shrinks while debt remains outstanding; continued acquisitions/distributions would impede repayment and increase refinancing dependence. Observable triggers are margin compression, CFO/sales convergence toward the cohort, advance/deferred-revenue reversal, growing receivable-sale reliance, capex persistently above cash generation, or renewed debt-funded cash uses. These are monitoring conditions, not unsupported forecasts or numerical covenant triggers. Conversely, repeated cash retention and a falling consistently defined debt/CFO burden would weaken the adverse financial-policy interpretation.
